title: Mexico’s Public Education Secretariat Orders Closure of Militarized Schools Before August 31
author: La Jornada Editorial Staff and Martín Hernández
content:
_This article by La Jornada Editorial Staff and Martín Hernández originally
appeared in the[July 29, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/07/29/estados/sep-ordena-el-
cierre-de-todas-las-escuelas-militarizadas-antes-de-iniciar-el-ciclo-
escolar-20262027), Mexico's premier left-wing daily newspaper._

The Secretariat of Public Education (SEP) informed all state education
authorities across the country that, for the start of the 2026-2027 school
year on August 31,**it must be guaranteed that no institution provides
educational services under a militarized or military denomination or
modality** , or any other that makes reference to instruction or discipline of
a military nature.

The agency stressed that, based on its constitutional powers and the General
Education Law, the head of the SEP, Mario Delgado Carrillo, asked the state
education secretariats to carry out an exhaustive review of all
authorizations, permits, and official recognitions of study validity (RVOE)
that have been issued in their respective states.

In cases where institutions operating under the aforementioned type of
denominations or modalities are detected,** "the suspension of their
activities will proceed and the corresponding administrative procedures must
be initiated for their definitive closure."**

Likewise, the immediate delivery of school documentation must be ordered for
students who might be affected, including full or partial certificates and any
other document held by the schools, in order to guarantee the continuity of
their academic path and facilitate their incorporation into another
educational alternative.

In the event that payments have been made for services yet to be rendered,
such as re-enrollments, school supplies, uniforms, or any other item, these
must be immediately refunded by the schools.

![](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/07/16970-1024x683.webp)Students from the Ignacio Zaragoza
Military Academy in Puebla during a march last year as part of their physical
activities in a forested area of ​​Puebla. Photo from the military academy's
Facebook page.

## 'Training Exclusive to the Defense Secretariat'

The federal agency emphasized that providing services under military
denominations or modalities "is incompatible with the aims and principles" of
the National Education System, since **military education is limited to the
training of members of the armed forces and the National Guard, and is
provided exclusively by the Secretariat of National Defense (Defensa).**

The head of the SEP's Unit of Legal Affairs and Regulation, Eurípides Flores
Pacheco, announced that since Monday the agency had notified the Education
Secretariat of the State of Puebla to begin the corresponding administrative
process to suspend the activities of the Academia Militarizada Ignacio
Zaragoza, located in the state capital.

In an interview, Flores Pacheco explained that the SEP carried out a review in
coordination with the 25th Military Zone and confirmed that the aforementioned
institution is the only one detected in Puebla that publicly promotes itself
under the military scheme and does not have a permit to operate with those
characteristics.

![Cadets in beige uniforms marching in formation with rifles on a
plaza](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/07/02-cadets.jpg)Photo: La Jornada

Governor Alejandro Armenta assured that the state government will act in
accordance with the law and with the resolution issued by the federal
authorities. During a press conference held yesterday in Mexico City, he
indicated that his administration will seek alternatives to prevent enrolled
students from losing the school year or having their education interrupted.

Sources close to the Ignacio Zaragoza academy have indicated that its
representatives are considering filing an amparo lawsuit to prevent the
suspension of activities.

Meanwhile, an audio recording attributed to the school's director, Daniel
Guzmán, is circulating on social media, in which he asserts that the school
will resort to the corresponding legal remedies to prevent its eventual
closure. "We are not going to sit idly by," the director states in the
aforementioned recording, which was supposedly obtained during a meeting he
held with mothers and fathers between Monday and Wednesday.

As of this edition's press time, the school had not officially confirmed the
authenticity of the audio.

The SEP's decision to close this type of educational center comes after the
alleged femicide of 13-year-old minor Dafne Zapata on July 16, during a camp
organized by the Academia Militarizada de Marina Doenitz, in Ciudad Madero,
Tamaulipas.
